headline: South Asia: Riyadh airport hit by fresh Houthi strike day after deadly attack
script:
Good evening. This is your global conflict briefing.

- South Asia: Riyadh airport hit by fresh Houthi strike day after deadly attack.

The Caribbean - bottom line: KIDD LANE  TERROR - Mom grieves for daughter who begged for help as triple murder rocks St Andrew community, forces residents to flee.
- Jamaica Gleaner, 18 hours ago: KIDD LANE  TERROR - Mom grieves for daughter who begged for help as triple murder rocks St Andrew community, forces residents to flee.
The frantic voice of her daughter pleading for help over the telephone moments before she was killed will forever haunt Natasha Hall. Hall’s daughter, 30-year-old Lashane Ellis, and her one-year-old grandson, Kaheel Daley, were killed on Friday night when armed men went to their home on Kidd Lane, off Spanish Town Road in St Andrew, opened fire and set the house ablaze. Before fleeing, the gunmen reportedly opened fire on a neighbouring house, killing 39-year-old Kimeisha Gibson.

Zaporizhzhia was hit by deadly Russian airstrikes on Saturday, 10 October, killing at least 17 people, including three children, Ukrainian officials said. Rescuers searched rubble for survivors as the city faced renewed strikes on residential areas.

ASIA
South Asia - bottom line: Riyadh airport hit by fresh Houthi strike day after deadly attack.
- Dawn (Pakistan), Times of India - Top Stories, Jerusalem Post, South China Morning Post - China, NDTV - Top Stories, Taipei Times, Al Jazeera - Middle East, just now: Riyadh airport hit by fresh Houthi strike day after deadly attack.
A fresh Houthi strike hit Riyadh’s international airport on Sunday, a day after another attack claimed by the Yemeni group killed at least a dozen people and forced authorities to suspend operations at the facility. Saturday’s attack, the deadliest on Saudi soil in more than a decade, was a sharp escalation in the Yemen war, where Riyadh backs the internationally recognised government against the Houthis.
- Dawn (Pakistan), 7 hours ago: FO reiterates Pakistan's 'firm and unshakeable' commitment to Saudi Arabia's security after Riyadh attack.
The Foreign Office (FO) on Sunday condemned a fresh wave of Houthi attacks against Saudi Arabia, reaffirming Pakistan’s “firm and unshakeable” commitment to the sovereignty, territorial integrity, security and stability of the Gulf state under the Makkah Joint Defence Agreement. The defence pact, of which Turkiye is also a part, was signed on August 7 and aims to strengthen collective deterrence and empower its signatory states to treat an attack against one of them as an attack against all of them.
- Dawn (Pakistan), 4 hours ago: KP Governor's Rule: An emergency in the street and state.
Back in 2024, the political future of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, and perhaps of Pakistan itself, looked like a coin toss. There were two broad possibilities. One was a grand political settlement, perhaps involving a period of exile for Imran Khan, with the United Kingdom replacing Saudi Arabia as the preferred destination. The other was the eventual termination of the last PTI provincial government through constitutional intervention. One of these possibilities has now materialised.
- Dawn (Pakistan), 5 hours ago: Maaz Sadaqat, Imran Randhawa star as Pakistan thrash Sri Lanka in second T20I to seal series.
Maaz Sadaqat hit a blistering 96 before Imran Randhawa’s miserly spell helped Pakistan thrash Sri Lanka by 82 runs in the second Twenty20 International and seal the three-match series for the hosts here at the Rawalpindi Cricket Stadium on Sunday. Both Maaz and Imran were able to make a match-winning impact in what was only their second T20I outing after making their debuts in Friday’s opening match.

The previous day, Saudi Arabia resumed strikes on Yemen’s Iran-allied Houthi rebels after a four-year ceasefire collapsed. Russian strikes hit multiple Ukrainian power plants on Sunday after US President Donald Trump’s claim that both sides had agreed to stop hitting each other’s energy infrastructure, Ukraine’s President Volodymyr Zelensky said. Zelensky, in a post on social media, said a drone had hit a Kyiv power plant, leading to power cuts in the capital. Taiwan’s military is grappling with a worsening manpower shortage, with its volunteer staffing rate remaining below the 80 per cent target for a third consecutive year and concerns mounting over the impact on combat readiness, according to the island’s legislature. The tanker MT PETRO DOLPHIN faced an assault while anchored off the coast of Sohar, Oman, with 11 Indian crew aboard. While nine crew members were successfully rescued, two remain unaccounted for. Local Coast Guard authorities have mobilized search-and-rescue operations, with ongoing efforts to find the missing crew members. Minister Sarbananda Sonowal has pledged full support for the rescue efforts underway.
- Times of India - Top Stories, 5 hours ago: Iran calls US response to seven-day Hormuz proposal ‘insufficient’.
Iran’s Supreme National Security Council secretary Mohsen Rezaei stated that the US response was insufficient to Iran's conditions. Tehran proposed a seven-day plan to reopen the Strait of Hormuz and resume nuclear negotiations. Foreign Minister Seyyed Abbas Araghchi indicated that the negotiations are ongoing, with messages exchanged through mediators. As tensions rise, Washington reportedly prepares military options against Iran amid ongoing discussions.
